business_problem: Siemens needed a scalable, secure product lifecycle platform that could connect previously isolated teams and data while opening a path for AI-assisted issue capture and faster manufacturing decisions.
solution_summary: Siemens deployed Teamcenter on Azure to give customers full visibility across planning, manufacturing, and purchasing, replacing siloed data and disconnected teams with a more adaptable product lifecycle management platform. Key components include Siemens Teamcenter acts as the core PLM system for planning, manufacturing, purchasing, and product collaboration; Azure hosts Teamcenter with the scale, security, and reliability needed for global manufacturing customers; OpenAI parses spoken shop-floor issues into structured fields that can be routed into the PLM workflow. Siemens gives customers a more connected PLM experience, can scale Teamcenter globally on Azure, and is using the partnership to accelerate go-to-market while building an AI roadmap for better manufacturing efficiency and customer experience.

evidence_quotes: With Teamcenter, customers can have full visibility up and down the product lifecycle, from planning, to manufacturing, to purchasing.
Manufacturing staff that see an issue can speak directly into their phone where OpenAI will immediately parse that information out and get it into the appropriate field.
Teamcenter on Azure combines Siemens's own industry-leading technology with the scalability, security, and reliability of Azure Cloud Services.
